title.narrative: Strengthening nutrition services delivery anticipatory action for projected La Nino and drought affected communities in Dhobley district

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2024 (HNRP) projects a critical situation with approximately 6.9 million people in need of humanitarian assistance, despite an overall reduction need in 2023. The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis further indicates an estimated 4 million (21 percent of population) are in IPC Phase 3 or worse (Crisis or Emergency). An estimated 1.7 million children under five are projected to face acute malnutrition in 2024, including 430,000 who are likely to be severely malnourished. High levels of acute food insecurity and malnutrition are expected to remain high in Somalia in 2024 and possibly worsen with the anticipated La Niña and extended drought in the coming seasons Similarly, estimated levels of acute are at a critical level at a GAM rate of 13% and a SAM rate of 1.8%. Also, the anticipatory projections shows that it will continue to have a serious level of acute malnutrition into the next session because of poor food security, low average rainfall and the increased burden of drought, floods and other climatic shocks. ltbrgtHowever, in anticipation of La Nino and existing drought SRDI plan to provide adequate screening and identification of acute malnutrition among children, pregnant and lactating women including training of community health workers to conduct routine and active case finding of malnutrition cases, promotion of Family/Mother MUAC for mothers and caregivers will be trained to screen their children, quarterly mass MUAC screening in Dhobley project locations and screening of newly arrived IDPs in collaboration with CCCM cluster and other partners, this will further enhance area based coordination and referral of the beneficiaries into different programs ltbrgtOptimal nutrition and care practices for mothers, infants and young children will be promoted through a variety of strategies, such as the formation of mother-to-mother support groups, face-to-face counselling from community health workers, the utilization of interactive media, such as Radio station talk show, community plays and the application of IEC/BCC materials amongst others. Integrating key messaging on topics such as hygiene and sanitation, health, immunization, and other related topics will be a part of the promotion of IYCF, additionally, SRDI will conduct Promotion campaign on “one egg per child per day” to ensure enhancement of local nutrition-sensitive agriculture and household food production. The prevention of malnutrition will also include the promotion and provision of micronutrient supplementation. Further to this, SRDI will provide treatment of severely acute malnourished children through therapeutic supplementation as well as referral of complicated severely cases to Dhobley Stabilization center.ltbrgt To ensure that the community owns the project, a variety of strategies that strengthen the accountability of affected people will be implemented. These strategies include community response and feedback sessions, engaging the community through innovative approaches such as telephone surveys and other methods to inform and gather information from the communities that are being targeted. The project will include the implementation of the Child Protection and Nutrition Integration Framework which will include the training of nutrition workers to identify and refer cases of child abuse and neglect.
